doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend, Philip Baldwin, Vice-President, Government and Public Affairs of the Aerospace Industries Association of Canada (AIAC), or to give preferential treatment to the AIAC, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to the AIAC. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my friend’s private interests.
This screen is administered by the Director of Policy and Operations to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my friend’s private interests. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friend’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
My Secretary of State, Chief of Staff, colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.

In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friends, Mr. David Friedland, Director of the Transportation Infrastructure and Strategic Industries at Global Public Affairs, Mr. Michel Breau, Associate Vice President at Wellington Dupont Public Affairs, and Mr. Wesley Boyd Senior Consultant at Crestview Strategy, or to give preferential treatment to their employers, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to my friends, or their employers.
I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my friends’ private interests.
This screen is administered by the Director of Policy to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my friends’ private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friends’ private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
My minister, chief of staff, parliamentary secretary, colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my brother, Mr. Graham Fox, Head of Government and Public Affairs with Dominion Dynamics or to give preferential treatment to Dominion Dynamics or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to my brother and his employer. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator knows or reasonably should know to affect my brother’s private interests or those of Dominion Dynamics or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates.
This screen is administered by my Chief of Staff to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my brother or his employer Dominion Dynamics’ private interests. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my brother or his employer’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Senior Associate Deputy Minister.
My minister, colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend, Mr. James D. Irving, President and Chief Executive Officer of J.D. Irving Limited, including J.D. Irving Limited its subsidiaries, affiliates, associates, divisions and or any legal form of business, (collectively, Mr. Irving’s business interests) or to give preferential treatment to any of them, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to my friend’s private interests including his business interests. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or my administrator know or reasonably should know to affect Mr. Irving’s interests.
This screen is administered by my Chief of Staff and by the Deputy Minister of Intergovernmental Affairs, to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving Mr. Irving’s interests. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect Mr. Irving’s interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Minister of Energy and Natural Resources.
The Prime Minister of Canada, the Chief of Staff to the Prime Minister of Canada, the Clerk of the Privy Council and Secretary to the Cabinet, the Deputy Clerk of the Privy Council and Associate Secretary to the Cabinet, the Deputy Secretary to the Cabinet (Governance), the Deputy Minister of International Trade, the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Canada to the United States of America, the Chief Trade Negotiator for Canada, the Associate Assistant Deputy Minister, Trade Policy and Negotiations, the Parliamentary Secretary to the President of the King’s Privy Council for Canada and Minister responsible for Canada-U.S. Trade, Intergovernmental Affairs and One Canadian Economy (Canada-U.S. Trade), the Parliamentary Secretary to the President of the King’s Privy Council for Canada and Minister responsible for Canada-U.S. Trade, Intergovernmental Affairs and One Canadian Economy (Intergovernmental Affairs and One Canadian Economy), the Leader of the Government in the House of Commons, my ministerial staff members and other necessary ministerial staff and public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist the public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate measure aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my brother, Mr. Jean-Sébastien Joly, Intelcom Courrier Canada Inc., Dragonfly Shipping, or Amazon while I exercise my duties and functions as Minister of Industry and Minister responsible for Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion, decision, debate or vote in relation to my brother, Intelcom Courrier Canada Inc., Dragonfly Shipping, or Amazon. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my brother’s private interests.
This screen is co-administered by the Deputy Minister of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada and my Chief of Staff to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor a participant in any discussions or decision-making processes pertaining to the private interests of my brother or of his companies, unless the interest in the decision or matter is one of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my brother’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
The Prime Minister of Canada, the Clerk of the Privy Council and Secretary to Cabinet, the Parliamentary Secretaries to the Minister of Industry as well as the members of my ministerial staff have been informed in writing of this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner of any additional matters I am made aware of in the future that should form part of the subject matter of this screen.
In the event that any relevant matter is not caught by the screen and comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Conflict of Interest Act to recuse myself from that issue or matter and inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner.

Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act, Ms. Deliah Bernard, former Senior Indigenous Affairs Advisor in the Office of the Prime Minister, has been granted a reduction of her limitation period under section 36 to permit her to accept a contract with the Assembly of First Nations (AFN).
Ms. Bernard applied for a reduction of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following their last day in office. The reduction allows Ms. Bernard to accept a contract with AFN.
In reviewing Ms. Bernard’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which include the following:
The general employment prospects of the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder:
- Ms. Bernard is specialized on the subject matter and offers unique experience in issues of great relevance to all parties involved.
The nature and significance to the Government of Canada of the information possessed by the former reporting public office holder by virtue of that office holder’s public office:
- The contract with the AFN does not overlap with the responsibilities she held in her previous role as a reporting public office holder.
The degree to which the new employer might gain unfair commercial advantage by hiring the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder:
- Ms. Bernard will not be expected to negotiate nor make representations to federal government on behalf of the AFN. There is no competition nor commercial advantage to be gained by hiring Ms. Bernard. Her role will be to provide advice on prioritizing and ranking issues of discussion with the premiers, with the objective of strengthening relationships between First Nations and provincial and territorial governments.
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the reduction in relation to Ms. Bernard’s contract with the AFN outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore waived the limitation period.
All other post-employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the duration of Ms. Bernard’s limitation period.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
As part of compensation from previous positions, I currently own restricted share units of Portland General Electric Co. and shares of The Chemours Co. These shares cannot be immediately divested because the Portland General Electric Co. shares have not reached their vesting date, and the shares of The Chemours Co. are in a black-out period.
It has been agreed that until these assets can be divested, the corporate books have been updated so that any communication or other information relating to these assets will not be sent to me but to the Trustee of my Blind Trust.
During such time, the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that, as required by section 21 of the Conflict of Interest Act, I will recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to Portland General Electric Co. and The Chemours Co. and their subsidiaries, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further my own private interests, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
I understand that recusal means that I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I know or reasonably should know to affect my private interests.
I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.
The shares of Portland General Electric Co. will be immediately sold in an arm’s-length transaction within 10 business days following the date of vesting.
The shares of Chemours Co. will be immediately sold in an arm’s length transaction within 10 business days of the date of the end of the black-out period.
This compliance measure will remain in force until the Commissioner notifies me in writing that it is no longer applicable following receipt of proof of divestment of the shares of Portland General Electric Co. and The Chemours Co.

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my spouse employed with the United Food and Commercial Workers union (UFCW Canada) or to give preferential treatment to UFCW Canada while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to UFCW Canada. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be.
I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my spouse’s private interest.
This screen is administered by the President and the Registrar of the Canada Industrial Relations Board to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my spouse’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my spouse’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
The members of the staff of the Canada Industrial Relations Board and my colleagues have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend, Mr. Rob Moore, Partner of Crestview Strategy, or to give preferential treatment to Crestview Strategy, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion, decision, debate or vote in relation to my friend and Crestview Strategy. I understand that recusal means?I must remove myself from?the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my friend’s private interests.
This screen is co-administered by my Chief of Staff and the Deputy Minister of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my friend’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friend’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
This screen does not restrict me from participating in any discussion, decision, debate or vote related to a client of Crestview Strategy.
Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Minister of Industry and Minister responsible for Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions.
The Prime Minister of Canada, the Clerk of the Privy Council and Secretary to Cabinet, the Parliamentary Secretary, the members of my ministerial staff, as well as necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

I understand that recusal means?I must remove myself from?the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my friend’s private interests.

This screen is co-administered by my Chief of Staff and the Associate Deputy Minister of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my friend’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friend’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
This screen does not restrict me from participating in any discussion, decision, debate or vote related to a client of Summa Strategies.

Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Minister of Industry and Minister responsible for Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions.

The Prime Minister of Canada, the Clerk of the Privy Council and Secretary to Cabinet, the Parliamentary Secretary, the members of my ministerial staff, as well as necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.

I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.

In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friends, Amaryllis Harrison and Stéphanie Blackett, employed with PAA Advisory or to give preferential treatment to PAA Advisory while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to PAA Advisory. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be.
I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my friends’ private interest.
This screen is administered by the Director of Policy in the Quebec Lieutenant’s Office to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my friends’ private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friends’ private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
My Minister, my colleagues, and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

The name of the individual should not be disclosed pursuant to subparagraph 51(2)(b)(vi) of the Conflict of Interest Act which reads as follows:
51 (2) If a public office holder has recused himself or herself in respect of a matter and a public declaration is made in respect of that recusal under subsection 25(1) or section 30,
(b) no publication of the declaration shall include any detail that could reveal, directly or indirectly, any of the following:
(vi) information that could reasonably be expected to cause injury to the privacy interests of an individual.

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further my private interests or to improperly further those of the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC), or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion, decision, debate or vote in relation to CIBC. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect CIBC’s interests.
This screen is co-administered by the Deputy Minister of Public Services and Procurement, the Chief Executive Officer of the Defence Investment Agency and my Chief of Staff to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving CIBC, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect CIBC’s interests as a member of a broad class unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Minister of Government Transformation, Public Works and Procurement.
The Prime Minister, the Minister of National Defence, the Minister of Industry, the Minister of Finance and National Revenue, the Clerk of the Privy Council and Secretary to the Cabinet, my Parliamentary Secretary, members of my ministerial staff, other necessary ministerial staff and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to my friends and their employers. I understand that recusal means that I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my friends’ private interests.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend employed by the Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA), or to give preferential treatment to CIJA, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to CIJA. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my friend’s private interests.
This screen is administered by the Director of Quebec, Francophone and Legal Affairs to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my friend’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friend’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Any matter that requires my involvement will be brought to the attention of the Deputy Minister or the Associate Deputy Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada to identify the appropriate course of action.
My Minister, direct reports, colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friend employed by the Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA), or to give preferential treatment to CIJA, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to CIJA. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrators know or reasonably should know to affect my friend’s private interests.
This screen is co-administered by the Deputy Chief of Staff and Director of Policy and the Senior Policy Advisor to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my friend’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my friend’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Any matter that requires my involvement will be brought to the attention of the Deputy Minister or the Associate Deputy Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada to identify the appropriate course of action.
My Minister, direct reports, colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter, by leaving the room or the virtual meeting where the discussion and decision making is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act, Ms. Scieur-Aparicio, former Director of Communications in the Office of the Minister of National Revenue, has been granted a reduction of her limitation period under section 36 to permit her to accept employment with Affaires Politiques, a public relations firm.
Ms. Scieur-Aparicio applied for a reduction of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following their last day in office. The reduction allows Ms. Scieur-Aparicio to accept a employment with Affaires Politiques.   In reviewing Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which include the following:
- Circumstances of departure: Ms. Scieur-Aparicio departed public office after less than two months.
- General employment prospects: Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s employment prospects are limited given her expertise and region of residence.
- Degree to which the new employer might gain unfair commercial advantage: No unfair advantage is envisaged since the duration in the position was very short and Ms. Scieur-Aparicio had no influence on the development of policies.
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the reduction in relation to Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s employment with Affaires Politiques outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore waived the limitation period.
All other post-employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the duration of Ms. Scieur-Aparicio’s limitation period.

Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my father, President of the Board of Directors of Bionest Technologies, of Bionest Technologies, its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to my father or to Bionest Technologies, its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be.
I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or my administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my father’s private interest.
This screen is co-administered by my Chief of Staff and Deputy Minister to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my father's private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my father's private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Secretary of State (Canada Revenue Agency and Financial Institutions).

Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.

Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to Counsel. I understand that recusal means that I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be.
I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my relative’s private interest.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder, to further the private interests or to give preferential treatment to the following entities:
-	Bruyère Health and its Research Institute
-	University of Ottawa
-	Université de Montréal’s affiliated hospital research centre.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to these entities or their representatives. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect the private interests of these entities.
This screen is co-administered by the Executive Vice-President and the Vice-President, Research – Programs of the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving the private interests of these entities. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect the private interests of these entities as members of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
The Minister of Health as well as the members of the Governing Council, the Executive Management, the Scientific Directors and staff members of the CIHR have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act, Mr. Yves Giroux, Parliamentary Budget Officer, has been granted a waiver of his limitation period under section 36 to enable him to accept a short-term contract with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
Mr. Giroux applied for a waiver of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following their last day in office. The waiver allows Mr. Giroux to accept a short-term contract with the OECD.
In reviewing Mr. Giroux’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which include the following:
-	 the circumstances under which the reporting public office holder left his or her office:
Mr. Giroux’s seven-year mandate ends September 2, 2025.
-	the nature, and significance to the Government of Canada, of information possessed by the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder by virtue of that office holder’s public office;
The contract with the OECD does not require the use of confidential or material information in order to be carried out.
-	the degree to which the new employer might gain unfair commercial advantage by hiring the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder:
The OECD is an international organization which does not have a commercial purpose. The OECD aims to promote cooperation and benefits all its members, including Canada. Mr. Giroux’s contract would not provide the OECD an unfair commercial advantage.
-	the authority and influence possessed by the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder while in public office:
The Office of the Parliamentary Budget Officer is recognized for its expertise and Mr. Giroux’s contract with the OECD would serve the public interest by allowing Canada’s expertise to be shared with other partner countries.
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the waiver in relation to Mr. Giroux’s short-term contract with the OECD outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore waived the limitation period.
All other post-employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the duration of Mr. Giroux’s limitation period.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my relative, Mr. Eric Paul, Executive Director of Operations for Sipekne’katik First Nation, or give preferential treatment to Sipekne’katik First Nation while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to my relative or Sipekne’katik First Nation. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the screen administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my relative’s private interests.
This screen is administered by the Atlantic Regional Advisor to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my relative’s private interests, or Sipekne’katik First Nation’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my relative’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Any matter that requires my involvement will be brought to the attention of the Chief of Staff to identify the appropriate course of action.
The Minister of Crown-Indigenous Relations and its ministerial liaisons, colleagues and necessary public servants have all been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter by removing myself from the room where the discussion or decision is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further my interests or to improperly further those of Brookfield Asset Management, Brookfield Corporation, and Stripe Inc., and any company owned or controlled by them (“the Companies”) of which I am aware on the date that my blind trust was established. Attached hereto as Annex A is a list of all of the Companies of which I am aware.
This screen will prevent me from giving preferential treatment to any of the Companies while I exercise my official powers, duties, and functions as a reporting public office holder.
This screen is administered by my Chief of Staff and by the Clerk of the Privy Council to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving the Companies’ interests. I may, however, participate in a discussion or decision on a matter that is of general application or that affects the Companies’ interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
All powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the appropriate minister, as selected by the screen administrators.
All ministers, members of my ministerial staff and other necessary ministerial staff and public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter by removing myself from the room where the discussion or decision is taking place. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist them in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me in order to avoid the appearance of preferential treatment or any opportunity to further the private interests of my former employer, the Council of the Great Lakes Region (CGLR), or to give preferential treatment to it or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder. I understand that recusal means I must remove myself from the room, physically or virtually as the case may be.
Accordingly, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to the CGLR or its subsidiaries, affiliates and associates. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or my administrator know or reasonably should know to affect my former employer's private interest.
This screen is co-administered by my Chief of Staff and Executive Assistant to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my former employer’s private interests, unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my former employer’s private interests as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Chief Financial Officer and Director General of Corporate Services of the Canada Water Agency.
My minister, members of my staff, colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by a public office holder and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holder and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity to further the private interests of my friends Olivia Neil, director at Microsoft, Imraan Bashir, partner at KPMG and Matej Pivac, director, consulting expert at CGI, or to give preferential treatment to them while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder.
Accordingly, I have agreed to abstain from any discussion or decision in relation to any procurement process that could involve my friends or their employers. I also agree to not have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes affecting my friend’s interests.
This screen is to be administered by my Chief of Staff and the Assistant Deputy Minister (Chief Technology Officer) of Public Services and Procurement Canada to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decisions-making processes involving my friends’ private interests, unless the interest in the decision or matter is of general application.
Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Associate Deputy Minister of Public Services and Procurement Canada.
My Minister, Deputy Minister, Assistant Deputy Ministers, colleagues and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter.
I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.

doc: Public Declaration of Agreed Compliance Measures (Section 29)

fields.label: Description
fields.value:
(This declaration replaces the one published on 2023/11/20.)
Conflict of interest screens are preventive compliance measures, agreed upon pursuant to section 29 of the Conflict of Interest Act (Act) by public office holders and the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, to assist public office holders in avoiding conflicts of interest. Screens also seek to minimize the possibility of conflicts arising between the public duties of the public office holders and their private interests or those of their relatives and friends.
The Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and I have agreed that a conflict of interest screen is an appropriate compliance measure for me, aimed at preventing any opportunity, while I exercise my official powers, duties and functions as a reporting public office holder, to further the private interests of my spouse, Mr. John Knowlton, Senior Managing Director and Business Manager of OMERS Infrastructure Management, or to give preferential treatment to the following affiliates that have or may have dealings with the Government of Canada:
- OMERS Infrastructure Management
- OMERS Administration Corporation
- Alectra
- Bruce Power
- Next Bridge Infrastructure
- TeraNet
Accordingly, as I have done in the past, I have agreed to recuse myself from any discussion or decision in relation to the above-mentioned entities. I also agree not to have any communication with government officials in relation to any matter or decision-making processes which I or the administrators of the screen know or reasonably should know to affect my spouse's interests.
This screen is co-administered by the Deputy Minister of Transport, the Deputy Clerk of the Privy Council and Associate Secretary to the Cabinet as well as my Chief of Staff to ensure that I am neither made aware of nor participate in any official matters or decision-making processes involving my spouse’s interests unless the interest relates to a decision or matter that is of general application. I will participate in decisions or matters of general application and those that may affect my spouse’s interest as a member of a broad class of persons unless those interests are disproportionate to the other members of the class.
Moreover, all powers, duties and functions on matters that form part of this screen will be exercised by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry.
The Prime Minister, the Clerk of the Privy Council and Secretary to the Cabinet, the Assistant Deputy Minister, Office of the Deputy Minister of Intergovernmental Affairs, Multilateral Relations, the Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Transport and Internal Trade, my ministerial staff members and necessary public servants have been informed in writing about this conflict of interest screen.
I have undertaken to inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner at the earliest opportunity of all changes of which I become aware that relate to or should form part of the above list of matters caught by this screen.
In the event that I am made aware of a matter forming part of this screen or any such matter comes before me, I am required under section 21 of the Act to recuse myself from that matter. I must so inform the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner and, where appropriate, make a public declaration of recusal pursuant to subsection 25(1) of the Act.
